title: Hepatitis B Perinatal Prevention Cascade In High-Burden Countries
summary: Build a verified way to measure the hepatitis B perinatal prevention cascade from maternal HBsAg screening through prophylaxis, timely birth dose, infant-series completion, and impact validation without confusing policy or any-dose coverage with timely protection.
why_it_matters: Ministries of health, immunization technical advisory groups, maternal-newborn programme directors, and funders must decide whether to finance universal timely birth-dose delivery, maternal testing and antiviral prophylaxis, outreach for home births, or EPI-maternity data linkage. Verified cascade evidence would show which bottleneck deserves the next dollar while preventing procurement, stock, or policy records from being counted as delivered prevention.

success_metrics.target: Every output separates maternal screening, prophylaxis, birth-dose timing, infant-series completion, and impact validation denominators.
success_metrics.validation_method: Domain reviewer checks each measure dictionary and output table for event definition, numerator, denominator, time window, and missingness handling.

success_metrics.target: Every burden, pathway, or coverage statement links to a dated evidence record with method and explicit limitations.
success_metrics.validation_method: Run pnpm validate and spot-check each source identity, evidence type, date, method, and limitation in evidence.json.

success_metrics.target: At least one named country or health-system analysis identifies a replicated cascade bottleneck without issuing clinical instructions.
success_metrics.validation_method: Independent replicator reruns the analysis from documented inputs and confirms that the result is suitable only for reviewed programme or funding decisions.

success_metrics.target: No canonical output exposes personal data or ranks facilities, countries, or mothers before safety review.
success_metrics.validation_method: Red-team and field-reality reviewers check outputs.md, validation.md, and each proposed artifact for privacy, stigma, coercion, and misuse risks.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, infectious-disease domain review, red-team review of clinical and stigma misuse, field-reality review of immunization and maternal-newborn workflows, and independent replication for quantitative outputs.
